candidate_sources.README.md:
# Translation memory lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Options component observer disposal; shared cache injected into mounted component

checkpoints: Mount a fresh online-mode query while offline, remove its final observer while still offline, then reconnect; verify its signal-consuming query function cannot receive a live signal.
Repeat with refetchOnReconnect varied; the repair must remain effective independently of that option.
Queue paused continuation, remove the final observer before the Promise callback runs, then drain the callback; verify the same protection.
Verify that removing one of several observers preserves the shared fetch.
Verify unconsumed active background completion, consumed-work abort and state restoration, and rejection of late fulfillment from a cancelled attempt.
Verify synchronous initial entry, deferred paused continuation, network modes, focus gating, retries, and reuse of the shared cache after observer disposal.
forbidden_effects: An abandoned fresh online-mode query mounted and unmounted entirely offline later entering its signal-consuming query function with a live signal.
Making the repair depend on refetchOnReconnect.
Cancelling shared work merely because one observer departs while another remains.
Discarding supported unconsumed active background completion.
Allowing an old attempt's fulfillment to populate a newer attempt.
Changing tests, configuration, dependencies, or public interfaces.
lifecycle_identity: A cached query is shared by key and outlives individual observer scopes.
Each subscribe call creates a unique observer handle; final-observer departure is distinct from an individual observer departure.
Each attempt owns its controller, previous-state snapshot, settlement and completion identity.
Existing completion guards compare the captured attempt object with q.attempt and reject settled attempts.
Signal consumption is recorded by actual getter access on the shared query; it must not be fabricated merely because work is paused or observerless.

obligations.text: Repair the documented fresh online-mode offline mount/unmount case so reconnect cannot subsequently supply a live signal to that abandoned query's signal-consuming function, independently of refetchOnReconnect.
Apply the repair across both future resume scheduling and a continuation already queued before final-observer departure; deferred execution must not bypass the abandonment decision.
Preserve unique observer handles, per-key fetch sharing, inert unknown unsubscribe, and cache retention outside individual component lifetimes.

Preserve actual-access signal consumption and supported unconsumed active completion into cache after departure. Preserve physical abort of consumed work, restoration of previous data/status with idle fetch status, and settlement of the originating attempt.
Keep asynchronous completion associated with its originating attempt so cancelled or superseded fulfillment cannot mutate a newer attempt's data.
Preserve synchronous initial online entry, Promise-turn paused continuation, initial network-mode behavior, focus-dependent continuation, always/offlineFirst behavior, and supported retries.
Limit any subsequent Action to product source, preserving interfaces, dependencies, build/test configuration, and existing observable state projection around cancellation and subscription changes.

ordering_barriers: Final-observer departure must establish the required protection before reconnect or an already-queued continuation can enter the abandoned attempt with a live signal.
Preserve cancellation's existing order: mark the attempt settled and restore previous state before calling controller.abort(), then project the query. Abort can synchronously invoke signal listeners.
Deferred completion and continuation must validate their captured attempt before changing state or invoking further work.
Preserve the lazy getter's synchronous consumption recording before returning the originating attempt's signal.

Inspect host.queryFn, timer scheduling, abort listeners and project callbacks as callback-capable boundaries when assessing preservation; a lexical guard alone does not prove validity after such a boundary.
preservation: Public Session and component forwarding interfaces, snapshot shape, and pending/success/error plus idle/fetching/paused state semantics.
Shared fetches for multiple observers and cache reuse after component observer disposal.
Supported unconsumed active background completion and consumed-work cancellation restoration.
Originating-attempt controller and completion identity, including stale-completion isolation.
Existing cancellation and projection ordering observable through injected callbacks.
Network modes, focus behavior, retry behavior, dependencies and build/test configuration.
